Sweets 7.62 solvent for breaking in a barrel?

The idea is that you want the first bullets fired to abrade away the high points in the steel barrel which catch on the bullet jackets. For reasons that are not entirely clear to me, this requires that traces of copper bullet jacket, left behind on these high points, be scrubbed away between each of these critical first shots. That's why you use Sweets, which dissolves copper.

You can do it if you want; it won't hurt anything, and might help. Just remember not to soak the barrel in that stuff, it will eventually start to etch the steel after an extended period of time.

As for cleaning, I might not be the best guy to ask...

For a regular rifle - not a bechrest gun, or a competition gun - I generally don't clean the bores at all. They get a good cleaning the first day I bring them home, to get the grit and factory preservatives out, and so I can have a good look inside. After that, unless I'm using corrosive ammo, they get one patch wet with oil at the end of the day, and that's that.

Most of the time, the crud - the copper deposits, the lead, the carbon - is self-limiting, and what you have after five shots is what you have after 500. There's no rust, no additional wear from the cleaning rod or the brushes, no chemicals seeping into the stock. As an added bonus, the first shot of the day usually lands pretty close to where the rest of them will go.

If you're competing it's different, but if you're competing, everything is different.

Sometimes the chambers need to be cleaned out, you'll notice when the cartridge has some resistance going it. This happens pretty quickly with .22s but it happens eventually with centerfire guns. You can just hit it with a chamber brush and a little oil, wipe the oil out, and that's that.
